name: Kidney (renal cell) cancer
theme: the doublet era · the adjuvant honesty ledger

meta.title: Kidney cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Renal cell carcinoma (clear-cell and non-clear-cell), adult
meta.population: Adults with renal cell carcinoma - clear-cell as the main axis (the biology the whole evidence base was built on) with non-clear-cell (papillary, chromophobe) as an honestly thinner branch, and urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis rerouted to the LIVE bladder trainer (the registry's second reroute gate landing on a working page). The localized story is surgery plus the ADJUVANT HONESTY LEDGER: one adjuvant immunotherapy with a real overall-survival receipt (KEYNOTE-564 pembrolizumab, OS HR 0.62 - the only one) displayed beside its three named negative siblings (IMmotion010, CheckMate 914, PROSPER) and the two-month-old second arm (belzutifan + pembrolizumab, FDA 2026-06-12 on LITESPARK-022's DFS - details still secondhand). The metastatic story is the doublet era's central epistemological problem rendered as architecture: four excellent 1L regimens, ZERO head-to-head trials - so the 1L menu deliberately ties.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease whose 1L menu is four excellent answers and no comparison. THE NO-HEAD-TO-HEAD TIE is the spec's signature: nivolumab+ipilimumab (CheckMate 214: ITT median OS 55.7 vs 38.4 months at 67.7-month follow-up, verified), the three IO-TKI doublets (KEYNOTE-426 OS HR 0.68; CheckMate 9ER final OS HR 0.79; CLEAR final OS HR 0.79 with its crossover caveat - each verified in its OWN trial), and favorable-risk TKI monotherapy all carry ONE flagged shared ranking number, because cross-trial comparison is illegitimate and the trainer refuses to fake it -…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: AJCC TNM for stage; IMDC risk model for metastatic disease (six factors; favorable 0 / intermediate 1-2 / poor >=3 - the router the doublet era was built on); NCCN Kidney v1.2026 (secondhand - 403; a newer 2026 version may exist)
meta.response: RECIST 1.1; the doublet era's practical reads are the depth question (CR rates differ across regimens) and the two-ledger attribution problem (hold the TKI first - TKI toxicity resolves in days, an irAE does not)

Newly diagnosed.name: Nephrectomy (partial when feasible) - the curative anchor
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: an operation and a kidney's worth of nephron arithmetic - partial preserves function, and the anesthesia conversation is real in this comorbid population
Newly diagnosed.patient: For kidney-confined tumors: an operation - keeping as much kidney as possible - cures most people; the smallest tumors can sometimes simply be watched.
drugs: Partial/radical nephrectomy (active surveillance for small masses)

Newly diagnosed.name: Adjuvant immunotherapy (the honesty ledger - one OS receipt, three negatives, one new arm)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: KEYNOTE-564: NCCN category 1 (secondhand, v1.2026); belzutifan+pembro approved 2026-06-12 (details secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized - 564's DFS AND OS met (the only adjuvant IO OS win in RCC); the three negatives named; the new arm's details secondhand (labeled)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a preventive year of the immune ledger (permanent endocrinopathies included) - now potentially plus belzutifan's anemia and hypoxia signatures; the trade is re…
Newly diagnosed.patient: After surgery for higher-risk kidney cancer: a preventive immunotherapy year that - uniquely among the four times this idea was tested - proved longer life; a second combination option arrived this June.

Newly diagnosed.name: Nivolumab + ipilimumab (CheckMate 214 - the IO doublet, int/poor's original answer)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized, ~8-year maturity - verified in its OWN trial; the ranking number is the shared tie
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the pure immune ledger at doublet intensity - no TKI costs, the deepest tail, the hardest first season
Newly diagnosed.patient: The two-immune-drug answer: the longest track record, the best chance of a treatment-free deep remission, the hardest first months - one of four strong first choices whose differences are about fit, not rank.

Newly diagnosed.name: IO-TKI doublet (KEYNOTE-426 / CheckMate 9ER / CLEAR - pick by fit)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: 1L standard options across all IMDC groups (NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x3 - each verified in its OWN trial; no head-to-head exists (the tie is the honesty)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the immune ledger plus the TKI ledger, attributed by the hold-first maneuver - faster responses bought with daily-management costs
Newly diagnosed.patient: The immune-plus-targeted answers: three proven combinations that work fast and across every risk group - chosen among by side-effect shape and your particulars, never by a ranking that doesn't exist.

Newly diagnosed.name: TKI monotherapy (the favorable-risk nuance, kept honest)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: favorable-risk option (NCCN secondhand) - the nuance, not the default
Newly diagnosed.evidence: the doublet trials' own favorable-risk subgroups (directionally verified; exact HRs flagged)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the TKI ledger alone - no immune season, for the patients whose biology may not need one yet
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the most indolent-behaving spread disease: a single targeted tablet - because in this exact group the big combinations' survival edge nearly disappears, and starting gentler is honest medicine, not under-treatment.

Newly diagnosed.name: Non-clear-cell systemic therapy (SWOG 1500's receipt; the chromophobe honesty)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN non-clear-cell section (secondhand); SWOG 1500 the one randomized receipt
Newly diagnosed.evidence: randomized phase 2 (SWOG 1500, papillary) - labeled; chromophobe extrapolation named
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the chosen regimen's ledger - carried with the honesty that the evidence behind it is thinner than the clear-cell menu's
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the rarer kidney-cancer types: real options with honestly thinner evidence - one type (papillary) has its own proven drug; another (chromophobe) is treated by careful borrowing, and a trial is often the genuinely best answer.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; bone pain and hematuria care are the craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice - and in this disease's slowest forms it overlaps with watchful waiting.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Cabozantinib (METEOR - the 2L receipt)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized (METEOR) - OS met; era-mismatch honesty carried
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the full TKI ledger at cabozantinib intensity - the dose-holding craft earns its keep here
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: When the first combination stops working: the proven next tablet, with real survival evidence - and honest fine print that its trial ran in an earlier treatment era.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Belzutifan (LITESPARK-005 - the median-defying curve, taught)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: FDA-approved post-IO/post-TKI (2023-12-14, verified); the pending combination dated on the card
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized - PFS met with non-proportional hazards (the lesson), OS not met (labeled, never ranks)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: anemia and hypoxia - the HIF mechanism's honest signatures, monitored by design
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A newer tablet with an unusual honest story: on average it looks similar to the old option, but a real fraction of patients get long, durable control the averages hide - and the card explains exactly that.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after the proven lines is a real road, with bone protection and symptom craft as active care.

Heng et al. IMDC prognostic model: six factors (KPS <80, anemia, hypercalcemia, <1 yr dx-to-tx, neutrophilia, thrombocytosis) - favorable 0 / intermediate 1-2 / poor >=3; the router the doublet era was designed around. JCO 2009;27:5794-9 (PMID 19826129, pubmed-url-match)

Choueiri et al. KEYNOTE-564 OS: adjuvant pembrolizumab - OS HR 0.62 (CI 0.44-0.87, p=0.005) at 57.2-month follow-up: THE ONLY adjuvant IO overall-survival benefit in RCC. NEJM 2024 (PMID 38631003, pubmed-url-match; 30-mo DFS paper PMID 36055304, matched)

THE LEDGER'S NEGATIVES, kept visible: IMmotion010 (atezolizumab - no DFS benefit; Lancet 2022, PMID 36099926, matched); CheckMate 914 Part A (nivo+ipi - DFS missed; Lancet 2023, PMID 36774933, matched; Part B negative secondhand); PROSPER/EA8143 (perioperative nivolumab - negative; Lancet Oncol 2024, DOI 10.1016/S1470-2045(24)00211-0 - PMID NEVER MATCHED, flagged not guessed). Three same-idea failures beside the one success

LITESPARK-022: belzutifan + pembrolizumab adjuvant - FDA APPROVED 2026-06-12 (fda.gov page title verified via domain-restricted search; approval date and DFS HR SECONDHAND - confirm on the fda.gov page; ASCO GU 2026 LBA418). The adjuvant ledger's two-month-old second arm - details carried at their honest grade

CheckMate 214 (nivo+ipi, int/poor-designed): long-term verified - ITT median OS 55.7 vs 38.4 months at 67.7-month follow-up (PMID 35383908, pubmed-url-match; 4-yr PMID 33246931; primary NEJM 2018 PMID 29562145 - all matched). 8-year (OS HR 0.72 ITT / 0.69 int-poor, Ann Oncol 2024): publisher-verified, PMID FLAGGED. Its ranking number is the shared tie; these are its OWN receipts

KEYNOTE-426 (pembro+axitinib): extended follow-up - OS HR 0.68 (CI 0.55-0.85), median NR vs 35.7 months; PFS 15.4 vs 11.1 (HR 0.71). Lancet Oncol 2020 (PMID 33284113, pubmed-url-match; primary NEJM 2019 PMID 30779529, matched). 5-yr Nat Med 2025 (OS HR 0.84; favorable-risk HR ~1.1): DOI/PMC only - PMID FLAGGED. Its own receipts; the ranking number is the tie
CheckMate 9ER: nivolumab + cabozantinib 1L (Choueiri NEJM 2021)

CLEAR (pembro+lenvatinib): final prespecified OS verified - HR 0.79 (CI 0.63-0.99), medians 53.7 vs 54.3 months WITH the crossover/subsequent-therapy caveat said aloud. JCO 2024 (PMID 38227898, pubmed-url-match; extended follow-up PMID 36858721, matched). The famous primary PFS 23.9 vs 9.2 (HR 0.39) carried FLAGGED (primary PMID not re-pulled this sweep)
COSMIC-313 (cabo+nivo+ipi triplet, int/poor): PFS met, grade 3-4 toxicity heavier, OS not established at publication - the triplet's cautionary receipt. NEJM 2023 (PMID 37163623, pubmed-url-match)

Mejean et al. CARMENA: sunitinib alone NON-INFERIOR to cytoreductive nephrectomy + sunitinib (int/poor risk) - the trial that retired the reflexive nephrectomy. NEJM 2018;379:417-27 (PMID 29860937, pubmed-url-match)

Choueiri et al. METEOR final: cabozantinib vs everolimus post-VEGFR-TKI - OS 21.4 vs 17.1 months (HR 0.70, CI 0.58-0.85). Lancet Oncol 2016 (PMID 27279544, pubmed-url-match). The 2L receipt, with era-mismatch honesty carried
Motzer et al. Lenvatinib + everolimus (randomized phase 2): PFS 14.6 vs 5.5 months vs everolimus (HR 0.40). Lancet Oncol 2015 (PMID 26482279, pubmed-url-match)
TIVO-3: tivozanib vs sorafenib 3L/4L (Rini Lancet Oncol 2020)

Choueiri et al. LITESPARK-005: belzutifan vs everolimus (post-IO/post-TKI) - PFS HR 0.75 (CI 0.63-0.90) with IDENTICAL 5.6-month medians (non-proportional hazards: the tail the median cannot see - the card's statistics lesson); ORR benefit; OS co-primary NOT met. NEJM 2024 (PMID 39167807, pubmed-url-match). FDA 2023-12-14 (fda.gov page verified)

Jonasch et al. LITESPARK-004: belzutifan for VHL-disease-associated RCC/hemangioblastoma/pNET - the 2021 VHL indication. NEJM 2021 (PMID 34818478, pubmed-url-match; FDA approval-summary PMID 36722140)

LITESPARK-011 (belzutifan + lenvatinib vs cabozantinib, post-anti-PD-(L)1): design paper PMID 36752726 (matched). RESULTS SECONDHAND (ASCO GU 2026): PFS met (14.8 vs 10.7, HR 0.70), ORR 53% vs 40%, OS HR 0.85 NS - sNDA under review, PDUFA reported 2026-10-04. THE ONE-ITEM PENDING SHELF: dated, not carded; re-verify weekly

Pal et al. SWOG 1500/PAPMET: cabozantinib beat sunitinib on PFS in metastatic papillary RCC (crizotinib/savolitinib arms dropped for futility; the 9.0-vs-5.6-month medians carried FLAGGED - confirm before quoting). Lancet 2021 (PMID 33592176, pubmed-url-match). The thin branch's one randomized receipt

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

PEAK-1 (NCT07011719): casdatifan + cabozantinib vs placebo + cabozantinib, post-anti-PD-(L)1 clear-cell RCC (<=1 prior metastatic line, KPS >=80), phase 3, PFS primary, ~700 pts (Arcus; Dana-Farber/Yale/UCSD) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache mid-2026), registry re-check due

LITESPARK-033 (NCT07227402): belzutifan + zanzalintinib vs cabozantinib for recurrence during/within 24 months after ADJUVANT anti-PD-(L)1 (Hgb >=10 gate), phase 3 open-label, PFS primary (Merck/Exelixis; ASCO 2026 TPS4633) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache 2026-06), re-check due. The 564/022 era's new population, randomized

PROBE / SWOG S1931 (NCT04510597): ICI-combo 1L +/- cytoreductive nephrectomy, randomized at the 10-14-week response read, OS primary, ~302 pts (SWOG/NCI network) - WEB-VERIFIED but on a SEPTEMBER 2025 CACHE: the screen's stalest entry, re-check FIRST

BLAZE (NCT07187778): neoadjuvant belzutifan vs pembrolizumab vs the combination, resectable clear-cell RCC, randomized phase 2 (MD Anderson, started 2025-12) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache 2026-06), re-check due.
